topic: Standards and event signatures for mapping wallet actions to on-chain evidence (ERC-20/721/1155, EIP-2612, Permit2, WETH9, EIP-7702, EIP-6780, mempool replacement, Aave V3 Pool)

facts.value: keccak256(canonical signature) computed locally with pycryptodome Crypto.Hash.keccak (digest_bits=256)
facts.note: Every topic0 below was computed from the event's canonical ABI signature (names/indexed stripped, `uint`->`uint256`, enums->`uint8`) taken from the pinned source file named in that fact. ERC-20 Transfer result 0xddf252ad... matches the universally published constant, validating the method.

facts.value: event Transfer(address indexed _from, address indexed _to, uint256 _value)
facts.note: ERC-20 (Final). Verbatim rule: 'MUST trigger when tokens are transferred, including zero value transfers.' and 'A token contract which creates new tokens SHOULD trigger a Transfer event with the `_from` address set to `0x0` when tokens are created.' Log shape: 3 topics (topic0 + from + to), data = value. Note: eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-20 still renders it, but ethereum/EIPs marks it status: Moved; canonical text is now ethereum/ERCs.

facts.note: Verbatim: 'MUST trigger on any successful call to `approve(address _spender, uint256 _value)`.' 3 topics, data = value. Also emitted by EIP-2612 permit() (see below), so an Approval log alone cannot distinguish approve() from permit().

facts.value: event Transfer(address indexed _from, address indexed _to, uint256 indexed _tokenId)
facts.note: ERC-721 (Final), erc-721.md line 55. Same topic0 as ERC-20 Transfer (0xddf252ad...) because canonical signature is identical, but ALL THREE params are indexed => log has 4 topics and empty data; ERC-20 has 3 topics + 32-byte data. Doc: 'This emits when ownership of any NFT changes by any mechanism. This event emits when NFTs are created (`from` == 0) and destroyed (`to` == 0). Exception: during contract creation, any number of NFTs may be created and assigned without emitting Transfer. At the time of any transfer, the approved address for that NFT (if any) is reset to none.' OZ v5.1.0 IERC721.sol line 15 matches.

facts.value: event Approval(address indexed _owner, address indexed _approved, uint256 indexed _tokenId)
facts.note: erc-721.md line 61. Same topic0 as ERC-20 Approval (0x8c5be1e5...), but 4 topics (3 indexed) and empty data. Doc: 'This emits when the approved address for an NFT is changed or reaffirmed. The zero address indicates there is no approved address. When a Transfer event emits, this also indicates that the approved address for that NFT (if any) is reset to none.' OZ v5.1.0 IERC721.sol line 20 matches.

facts.value: function permit(address owner, address spender, uint value, uint deadline, uint8 v, bytes32 r, bytes32 s) external
facts.note: ERC-2612 (Final), lines 44-46 also define `nonces(address owner) returns (uint)` and `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() returns (bytes32)`. Verbatim semantics (lines 52-62): permit 'will set `allowance[owner][spender]` to `value`, increment `nonces[owner]` by 1, and emit a corresponding `Approval` event, if and only if': blocktime <= deadline; owner != zero address; `nonces[owner]` (before update) == nonce; (v,r,s) valid secp256k1 signature from owner over the EIP-712 message. 'If any of these conditions are not met, the `permit` call must revert.'

facts.value: NO new event; on-chain evidence is the standard ERC-20 Approval(owner, spender, value) log (topic0 0x8c5be1e5...) emitted by the token
facts.note: The spec text defines only functions and reuses EIP-20 Approval. Consequence for action mapping: a permit shows up as an Approval log where the tx sender is typically a relayer/spender, not the owner; the owner did not send any transaction. Distinguish from approve() only via the call trace (permit selector) - not from the log.

facts.value: keccak256("Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)") = 0x6e71edae12b1b97f4d1f60370fef10105fa2faae0126114a169c64845d6126c9
facts.note: erc-2612.md line 70 (struct typehash string, computed locally). This is an EIP-712 struct hash, NOT a log topic. Digest = keccak256(0x1901 || DOMAIN_SEPARATOR || keccak256(abi.encode(TYPEHASH, owner, spender, value, nonce, deadline))).

facts.value: permit(): reverts ERC2612ExpiredSignature(deadline) if block.timestamp > deadline; recovers signer via ECDSA over _hashTypedDataV4(structHash); reverts ERC2612InvalidSigner(signer, owner) on mismatch; then _approve(owner, spender, value) which emits Approval
facts.note: PERMIT_TYPEHASH in OZ is the same string as ERC-2612. nonces() delegates to Nonces; DOMAIN_SEPARATOR() returns _domainSeparatorV4(). Interface: contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Permit.sol lines 66-89 at the same tag.

facts.value: Uniswap/permit2 @ cc56ad0f3439c502c246fc5cfcc3db92bb8b7219 (main at time of research)
facts.note: README: 'Permit2 is the union of two contracts: AllowanceTransfer and SignatureTransfer. The SignatureTransfer contract handles all signature-based transfers, meaning that an allowance on the token is bypassed and permissions to the spender only last for the duration of the transaction that the one-time signature is spent. The AllowanceTransfer contract handles setting allowances on tokens, giving permissions to spenders on a specified amount for a specified duration of time.' Both modes require the user's ERC-20 approve() to the Permit2 contract first (an ordinary ERC-20 Approval log with spender = Permit2).

facts.note: IAllowanceTransfer.sol lines 32-39. Doc: 'Emits an event when the owner successfully sets permissions using a permit signature on a token for the spender.' topic0 = keccak256('Permit(address,address,address,uint160,uint48,uint48)') = 0xc6a377bfc4eb120024a8ac08eef205be16b817020812c73223e81d1bdb9708ec. 4 topics; data = (amount, expiration, nonce).

(direct approve() on Permit2, no signature). topic0 = keccak256('Approval(address,address,address,uint160,uint48)') = 0xda9fa7c1b00402c17d0161b249b1ab8bbec047c5a52207b9c112deffd817036b. NOT the ERC-20 Approval topic0 (different arity/types); emitted by the Permit2 contract, with `token` as topic2.

facts.value: event UnorderedNonceInvalidation(address indexed owner, uint256 word, uint256 mask)
facts.note: ISignatureTransfer.sol line 19; the ONLY event declared in ISignatureTransfer. Doc: 'Emits an event when the owner successfully invalidates an unordered nonce.' topic0 = keccak256('UnorderedNonceInvalidation(address,uint256,uint256)') = 0x3704902f963766a4e561bbaab6e6cdc1b1dd12f6e9e99648da8843b3f46b918d. Implication: a consumed SignatureTransfer permit (permitTransferFrom) leaves no Permit2-level log - only the token's ERC-20 Transfer(owner -> recipient) with msg.sender = Permit2 in the call trace.

Uniswap official docs deployments table lists Permit2 at this address on Ethereum mainnet and Sepolia; the Permit2 overview page (developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/permit2/overview) says it is deployed at this address 'on most networks' but zkSync uses 0x0000000000225e31D15943971F47aD3022F714Fa. The pinned repo README does NOT state the address. Per-chain confirmation for the chains this project indexes is an open question.

facts.value: gnosis/canonical-weth @ 0dd1ea3e295eef916d0c6223ec63141137d22d67 contracts/WETH9.sol (pragma solidity >=0.4.22 <0.6)
facts.note: Events declared lines 23-26: `event Approval(address indexed src, address indexed guy, uint wad); event Transfer(address indexed src, address indexed dst, uint wad); event Deposit(address indexed dst, uint wad); event Withdrawal(address indexed src, uint wad);`. deposit() (line 34) emits ONLY Deposit(msg.sender, msg.value) (line 36); withdraw(uint wad) (line 38) emits ONLY Withdrawal(msg.sender, wad) (line 42). No Transfer from/to 0x0 is emitted on wrap/unwrap, so ERC-20-Transfer-only mint/burn detection misses WETH supply changes; native ETH movement is visible only via value transfer / balance change in the trace.

facts.value: SET_CODE_TX_TYPE = 0x04; payload = rlp([chain_id, nonce, max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas, gas_limit, destination, value, data, access_list, authorization_list, signature_y_parity, signature_r, signature_s]); authorization_list = [[chain_id, address, nonce, y_parity, r, s], ...]
facts.note: EIP-7702 status Final (Prague/Pectra). MAGIC = 0x05, PER_AUTH_BASE_COST = 12500, PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST = 25000. Outer fields follow EIP-4844 semantics: 'this implies a null destination is not valid' (a type-4 tx cannot be a contract creation). 'The transaction is considered invalid if the length of `authorization_list` is zero.' Also invalid if any tuple field is out of bounds (chain_id < 2**256, nonce < 2**64, len(address)==20, y_parity < 2**8, r,s < 2**256). Receipt payload = rlp([status, cumulative_transaction_gas_used, logs_bloom, logs]). Also at https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702.

facts.value: authority = ecrecover(msg, y_parity, r, s) where msg = keccak(MAGIC || rlp([chain_id, address, nonce]))
facts.note: The 'authority' is the EOA whose code is being set - the signer of the tuple, NOT the tx sender (tx sender may be a sponsor). `address` in the tuple is the delegation target. 's' must be <= secp256k1n/2 (EIP-2). Step 4: authority is added to accessed_addresses (EIP-2929). Step 5: 'Verify the code of `authority` is empty or already delegated' (an EOA that already has real contract code cannot be delegated).

facts.value: Tuple `nonce` must equal the authority's current account nonce (step 6); after a valid tuple is applied the authority's nonce is increased by one (step 9). The authorization list is processed 'before the execution portion of the transaction begins, but after the sender's nonce is incremented.'
facts.note: Derived consequence (not quoted text): for a self-sponsored tx (sender == authority) the tuple nonce must be tx.nonce + 1, because the sender nonce is bumped first. 'When multiple tuples from the same authority are present, set the code using the address in the last valid occurrence.' Each valid tuple is therefore an on-chain nonce increment for the authority even though the authority sent no transaction.

facts.value: 'If any step above fails, immediately stop processing the tuple and continue to the next tuple in the list.' ... 'Note, if transaction execution results in failure (e.g. any exceptional condition or code reverting), the processed delegation indicators is *not rolled back*.'
facts.note: Two distinct facts for action mapping: (a) an invalid tuple (bad chain id, bad sig, nonce mismatch, authority has non-delegation code) is silently skipped without invalidating the transaction; (b) valid tuples' code+nonce changes persist even when the tx status is FAILED/REVERTED. So a delegation/revocation must be derived from the tuple outcome, not from tx status.

facts.value: code of authority := 0xef0100 || address (23 bytes). If address == 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000: 'do not write the delegation indicator. Clear the account's code by resetting the account's code hash to the empty code hash 0xc5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470.'
facts.note: Step 8. Uses banned opcode 0xef (EIP-3541) as a marker; 'CALL loads the code at `address` and executes it in the context of `authority`.' Wallet actions: 'delegate to smart account' = tuple with non-zero address; 'revoke delegation' = tuple with zero address. Evidence is a CodeChange on the authority (new code 0xef0100||addr or empty), not a log.

facts.value: 'discarded' is Firehose terminology, not EIP text: SetCodeAuthorization.discarded (field 1) - 'Discarded determines if this authorization was skipped due to being invalid. As EIP-7702 states, if the authorization is invalid (invalid signature, nonce mismatch, etc.) it must be simply discarded and the transaction is processed as if the authorization was not present in the authorization list.'
facts.note: type.proto lines 629-688: TransactionTrace.set_code_authorizations (field 36) 'will contain all the authorizations as they were specified in the transaction itself regardless of their validity'; SetCodeAuthorization fields: discarded (bool,1), chain_id (bytes,2), nonce (uint64,3), v (uint32,4), r (5), s (6), authority (optional bytes,7 - 'If the authority cannot be recovered from the signature, this field will be empty and the `discarded` field will be set to `true`'), address (bytes,8; note: was missing on early testnet/BSC/Arbitrum Sepolia activations, backfill promised). Header comment lines 72-80: 'nonce changes and code changes for each accepted authorization in the transaction should be recorded in the state even if the transaction fails ... both NonceChange and CodeChange entries will be present for each authorized account, with the transaction sender's nonce change appearing first without a corresponding code change.' This repo already consumes this: erc20/balances/src/persist.rs filters `!a.discarded`.

facts.value: Different tx than creation: frame halts; 'SELFDESTRUCT does not delete any data (including storage keys, code, or the account itself)'; transfers entire balance to target; self-target => no net change, Ether NOT burnt. Same tx as creation: prior behaviour - deletes data, transfers entire balance to target, sets caller balance to 0; self-target => Ether IS burnt. No refund (EIP-3529) in either case.
facts.note: EIP-6780 status Final, Cancun. 'A contract is considered created at the beginning of a create transaction or when a CREATE series operation begins execution (CREATE, CREATE2, and other operations that deploy contracts in the future). If a balance exists at the contract's new address it is still considered to be a contract creation.' Action-mapping consequence: post-Cancun a SELFDESTRUCT in a later tx is just a balance sweep (native value transfer to target) with code/storage intact - do NOT model it as 'contract deleted'; only same-tx create+selfdestruct removes code. Also at https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6780.

facts.value: EIP-1559 defines tx type 0x02 with max_priority_fee_per_gas and max_fee_per_gas but contains no text on transaction replacement, cancellation, or mempool/pending semantics
facts.note: Status Final. Replacement/cancellation is therefore not a protocol (consensus) concept; it is a client-local transaction-pool policy (see geth facts). The protocol only guarantees at most one included tx per (sender, nonce).

facts.value: --txpool.pricebump: 'Price bump percentage to replace an already existing transaction' (default: 10)
facts.note: Related: --txpool.lifetime 'Maximum amount of time non-executable transaction are queued' (default 3h0m0s); --txpool.accountslots default 16; --txpool.globalslots default 5120. These are node-operator settings, so whether a replacement is accepted varies per node - further evidence that replacement is not an on-chain fact.

facts.value: legacypool.Config.PriceBump: 'Minimum price bump percentage to replace an already existing transaction (nonce)'; DefaultConfig.PriceBump = 10; core/txpool/errors.go ErrReplaceUnderpriced = errors.New("replacement transaction underpriced")
facts.note: legacypool.go lines 150, 166, 767-770 ('Nonce already pending, check if required price bump is met' -> list.Add(tx, pool.config.PriceBump)); errors.go line 38. Pinned to go-ethereum master at research time (not a release tag). geth txpool RPC docs (https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/rpc/ns-txpool): 'there may be multiple transactions associated with the same account and nonce. This can happen if the user broadcast multiple ones with varying gas allowances (or even completely different transactions).' Dashboard docs (https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/monitoring/understanding-dashboards): 'executable replace: rate that valid transactions are replaced with a new one from same sender with same nonce but higher gas'.

facts.value: A 'speed-up'/'cancel' is a new transaction with the same sender nonce and >= pricebump% higher fees that displaces the earlier one in each node's local pool; only the transaction that is finally included appears in a block. The displaced tx leaves no on-chain trace, and a 'cancel' is indistinguishable on-chain from any ordinary tx at that nonce (commonly a 0-value self-transfer, but that convention is wallet UX, not protocol).
facts.note: Synthesis of EIP-1559 (silent), geth flag docs, geth source and txpool RPC docs above. For the requirements doc: 'replaced', 'dropped', 'cancelled' states can only be represented as absence of inclusion / a different tx consuming the nonce; a Firehose Extended block cannot evidence them.
